definition: Fragmentary means made up of small disconnected pieces.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word fragmentary. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know fragmentary should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: His memory of the crash is fragmentary - a horn, a blue fender, the smell of rain - with nothing joining the pieces.
An incomplete file is missing a page or two; fragmentary goes further down the scale of ruin - what survives is only scraps.
Patchy coverage has holes you can map; fragmentary is worse still: no stretch is whole, and the pieces barely touch.

Piecemeal describes how something arrives or gets built — one scrap at a time, over stretches of time, with no overall plan. Fragmentary judges what remains after the losses are counted: most of the whole is missing, and scraps are all that survive.

A disjointed account has all its parts on hand, but they fail to connect or flow — the telling lurches from scene to scene. Fragmentary faults survival instead: most of the whole is simply gone, and what is left cannot connect because it barely exists.

Fragmentary judges completeness, nothing else: the surviving record is scraps.
It pairs naturally with archives, memories, and fossils.
Set it against circumstantial, this unit's evidence word - circumstantial evidence is indirect but can be plentiful and whole; fragmentary evidence is direct but survives only in pieces.
